title: Split CI into selective build stages and roll-forward toolchain
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Problem summary:
Our monolithic CI pipeline runs a full matrix of steps for every PR which increases median feedback time and spend. Multiple teams have noisy, slow builds caused by heavy language toolchains, full image rebuilds, and poor cache locality. We also have drift across developer toolchains (local vs CI) causing subtle build/test flakes.

Goal:
Split the pipeline into targeted, low-cost stages that run by default (fast feedback), with optional/full pipelines for releases and integration tests. Standardize and roll forward toolchains via immutable toolchain bundles and layered base images so cache hits are predictable. Reduce median PR CI wall time by ~40% and monthly CI cost by ~30% within the next sprint.

Approach / proposed changes:
1) Stage split (Buildkite pipeline):
   - fast-check: quick static checks (changed files diff), formatting, minimal lint, unit tests for touched packages (default for all PRs).
   - lint-gate: more expensive linters and style checks run asynchronously; can be marked as required for feature branches but optional for small doc fixes.
   - cache-warmup: populate remote CAS/BuildKit cache and language caches (pip wheels, node_modules, go/pkg) on merged commits to main.
   - full-build: heavy integration/instrumentation tests run on schedule/explicit trigger (release branches or nightly).

2) Toolchain roll-forward and base images:
   - produce immutable toolchain bundles (tar + manifest with sha256) per language (python, node, go, rust) stored in an internal artifact repo.
   - publish small layered base images: rwi/base:rootless, rwi/base:lang-python-3.11, rwi/base:lang-node-20, rwi/base:lang-rust-1.72. Each layer is independently cacheable.
   - CI references manifests (not ad-hoc apt/pip installs) to ensure hermetic builds.

3) Remote cache and selective artifact promotion:
   - adopt BuildKit remote cache (CAS) backed by an S3-friendly store + index; enable extract-only cache-on-success promotion from main branch builds.
   - integrate sccache for Rust and pip wheelhouse caching for Python, yarn cache for JS to avoid repeated fetches.

4) Developer ergonomics & gating:
   - provide local dev helper (rwi-dev image + run-local script) to mirror CI toolchain bundles.
   - pre-commit hooks for quick local lint to reduce server-side runs.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Increased complexity in CI orchestration and image publishing pipeline. Requires on-call learning and runbook updates.
- Cache invalidation edge cases when rolling toolchains; mitigated via staged rollouts and canary image tags.
- Upfront work to produce bundles and update Dockerfile references across ~40 repos.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Median PR wall-clock time reduced by >= 35% over baseline within 4 weeks of rollout.
- Monthly CI bill reduced by >= 25% (measured by cost dashboard tag).
- Flakiness rate (failed CI due to infra/toolchain) reduced to < 1% of PRs.
- Developers can reproduce CI image locally with the provided helper in < 10 minutes.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: prototype stage-split pipeline in one repo (platform/runtime), publish first toolchain bundle (python).
- Week 2: enable remote BuildKit cache and sccache proof-of-concept for rust crates; run main-build cache promotion.
- Week 3: roll to 10 high-velocity repos, add local dev helper and docs, gather metrics.
- Week 4: finalize image publishing automation, enable lint-gate orchestration, iterate on cache policies.

Operational runbook snippets:
- How to force a full rebuild: label PR with [ci rebuild-all] or trigger full-build manually in Buildkite.
- When to roll back a toolchain bundle: if >3 unrelated repos observe build-breaks within 24h, demote the bundle and promote previous manifest.

Notes on alternatives considered:
- Alternative A: Keep single pipeline but drastically parallelize steps. Rejected because it still runs all heavy steps for every PR and consumes more parallel capacity and cost.
- Alternative B: Trust only local dev caching. Rejected because developer environments vary and CI needs hermetic reproducibility for release builds.

Dependencies and follow-ups:
- Needs infra ticket to provision remote CAS bucket and index (infra ticket pending).
- Needs signing for published bundles (security coordination) — track with security_review_required flag.

Longer-term ideas:
- Auto-tune stage execution by analyzing changed paths (monorepo awareness).
- Cost-aware scheduling: queue heavy builds to low-cost regions during off-peak hours.
